title: Smooth Picard stack for algebraic-space curve families
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to S$ a morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] that is proper, flat and of finite presentation. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; flatness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts, and finite presentation includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. For each $S$-scheme $B$, put $X_B=X\times_SB$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Define $\mathcal P_f(B)$ to be the groupoid of line modules on the small etale site of $X_B$, meaning $\mathcal O_{X_B}$-modules etale locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{X_B}$, with module isomorphisms as arrows. For $u:B'\to B$ pullback is along the canonical ringed etale topoi: $u_X^*M=\mathcal O_{X_{B'}}\otimes_{u_X^{-1}\mathcal O_{X_B}}u_X^{-1}M$ [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Arrows over $u$ are isomorphisms $u_X^*M\cong M'$, and composition uses the canonical composition isomorphism of module pullback. Then $\mathcal P_f$ is an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. If every geometric fibre $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, has dimension at most one (dimension is the supremum of the Krull dimensions of affine etale charts [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$), then $\mathcal P_f$ is smooth over $S$: it admits a smooth surjective scheme atlas $a:V\to\mathcal P_f$ for which $V\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Surjectivity of this atlas means that every object of $\mathcal P_f$ over a field $K$ lifts to $V$ after some field extension $K\hookrightarrow K'$, with an isomorphism to the pulled-back object. No hypothesis on $f_*\mathcal O_X$, sections, reducedness, connectedness, nonempty fibres or Noetherian bases is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D04 (proposition-pic), for algebraicity with algebraic-space total space; moduli.tex Tag 0DPJ (lemma-pic-curves-smooth), under the standing algebraic-space hypotheses of section-picard-stack, and Tag 0DMB (lemma-pic-qs-lfp).

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-space-coherent-stack-general] for $f:X\to S$. Properness gives separatedness by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], so its hypotheses hold and $\mathcal C_{X/S}$ is algebraic and locally of finite presentation over $S$. The groupoid $\mathcal P_f$ in the statement is exactly $\mathcal L_{X/S}$ of [lem-sfb-space-invertible-open-coherent], with identical tensor pullbacks and arrows. That lemma realizes it as an open subcategory of $\mathcal C_{X/S}$. By [lem-sfb-open-stack-algebraic-lfp], $\mathcal P_f$ is algebraic and locally of finite presentation over $S$. This proves algebraicity without imposing a fibre-dimension bound.

Now assume the geometric fibre bound. To apply [lem-sfb-stack-infinitesimal-smooth-criterion], fix an arbitrary first order thickening $T=\operatorname{Spec}A\hookrightarrow T'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ of affine $S$-schemes and a line module $L$ on $Z=X_T$. Write $I=\ker(A'\to A)$, so $I^2=0$ and $A=A'/I$. Set $Z'=X_{T'}$. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], $Z'\to T'$ is flat, proper and finitely presented. Every geometric fibre is a geometric fibre from the hypothesis: a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T'$ composes to $S$, and its fibre product with $Z'$ is $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Thus $Z'\to T'$ is a family in [lem-sfb-curve-limit-preservation]. It suffices to extend $L$ to $Z'$.

source.place: Tag 0DPJ (lemma-pic-curves-smooth), reduction to affine first order thickenings

proof.text: Order the finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras $A'_i\subseteq A'$ by inclusion and put $I_i=I\cap A'_i$, $A_i=A'_i/I_i$, $T'_i=\operatorname{Spec}A'_i$, $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. By [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine], $T'=\varprojlim T'_i$ with affine transitions. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], all $T'_i$ are Noetherian. The ideals $I_i$ square to zero. The quotients $A_i$ inject into $A$, and their directed union is $A$: every element of $A$ has a lift in $A'$ contained in one $A'_i$. Thus $T=\varprojlim T_i$ by the affine spectrum universal property. Extension of $I_j$ need not equal $I_i$ for $i\geq j$; the stage thickenings are not asserted to form cartesian squares.

source.place: Tag 07SK (lemma-descend-finite-presentation); limits.tex Tag 01Z0 (lemma-noetherian-approximation), affine finitely generated subrings

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-curve-limit-preservation], after choosing a stage $i_0$ there is a flat proper finitely presented family $Z'_{i_0}\to T'_{i_0}$ with geometric fibres of dimension at most one whose pullback to $T'$ is $Z'$. For $i\geq i_0$ set $Z'_i=Z'_{i_0}\times_{T'_{i_0}}T'_i$ and $Z_i=Z'_i\times_{T'_i}T_i$. They have the same family properties by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. The $Z_i$ have affine transition maps, since the $T_i$ are affine, and limit $Z$, by the universal property of fibre products and inverse limits. They are quasi-compact and quasi-separated because they are proper over affine schemes. Apply [lem-sfb-space-invertible-limit-descent] to this inverse system: at some later stage $i$ there is a line module $L_i$ on $Z_i$ whose pullback is isomorphic to $L$. Notice that $T_i\hookrightarrow T'_i$ varies with $i$; it is not required to be the pullback of a fixed stage thickening.

Let $J_i$ be the ideal of $Z_i\hookrightarrow Z'_i$. This is a thickening by [lem-sfb-space-thickening-base-change], and on any affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}B'\to Z'_i$ it has ideal $I_iB'$, whose square is zero. Choose a jointly surjective family of such charts, each of finite type over the Noetherian affine $T'_i$, as permitted by local finite presentation on charts. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $B'$ is Noetherian. By [lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented], its ideal $I_iB'$ is finitely generated; since it is killed by itself, the same generators generate it over $B'/I_iB'$. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules], $J_i$ is a quasi-coherent ideal of $\mathcal O_{Z'_i}$, and since $J_i\cdot J_i=0$ it is the direct image of a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{Z_i}$-module, again written $J_i$: this is $J_i$ with the quotient action. The base changes $\operatorname{Spec}(B'/I_iB')\to Z_i$ of the chosen charts form a jointly surjective etale family, their rings are Noetherian as quotients of $B'$, and on them $J_i$ is associated to the finitely generated $B'/I_iB'$-module $I_iB'$. Hence $J_i$ is coherent in the sense of [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-fibre-cohomology-bound]. The scheme $T_i$ is Noetherian as the closed subscheme defined by $I_i$ of the Noetherian affine $T'_i$; equivalently its ring is a quotient of a Noetherian ring.

Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-fibre-cohomology-bound] with $p:Z_i\to T_i$, $d=1$ and $F=J_i$. The base is Noetherian, $p$ is proper and all its geometric fibres have dimension at most one; coherence was checked in Step 5. Thus $R^2p_*J_i=0$. Properness makes $p$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $T_i$ is affine, so [lem-sfb-space-affine-base-higher-image-sections] gives $H^2(Z_i,J_i)\cong\Gamma(T_i,R^2p_*J_i)=0$. Exactness of [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-picard-obstruction] now supplies a line module $L'_i$ on $Z'_i$ and an isomorphism $L'_i|_{Z_i}\cong L_i$.

Pull $L'_i$ back along $Z'\to Z'_i$. A tensor pullback of a line module is a line module: pull back its etale local trivializations, where $\mathcal O\otimes\mathcal O$ is the target structure sheaf. The resulting $L'$ restricts to $L$ because both composites $Z\to Z_i\to Z'_i$ and $Z\to Z'\to Z'_i$ agree, and the pullback composition isomorphisms identify the restriction with the pullback of $L_i$. Compose with the isomorphism in Step 4. This proves essential surjectivity for every affine first order thickening over $S$, including non-Noetherian ones. Step 1 supplies local finite presentation, so [lem-sfb-stack-infinitesimal-smooth-criterion] proves smoothness in precisely the atlas sense asserted. The field-extension formulation of surjectivity follows from [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus].
